fix: Read CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (keep the old name as a fallback), refuse or warn when no session id resolves rather than using 'none', and hash toplevel() instead of cwd.
text: Outside herdr the session id is read from $CLAUDE_SESSION_ID, which Claude Code does not export (it exports CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID; confirmed in this pane's env). Every Claude lane outside herdr in the same cwd gets agent 'session-none', so two lanes share one identity and one outbox, and check-reply cannot tell one lane's reply from the other's — the 'other lane' refusal the spec requires. The workspace also hashes os.getcwd() rather than the repo toplevel, so the same lane running check-reply from a subdirectory refuses its own reply.

fix: Re-read state after the POST and set only `sent` (write `sent` to a separate marker file, as events already do with .sent).
text: try_send reads the state file before the POST, which can take up to 3 s, and afterwards writes the whole state back with sent=True. A concurrent lane `close` or `stale` landing in that window gets overwritten with status 'open', which resurrects the packet, and check-reply then accepts a reply to a closed or stale packet. The driver flushes lane outboxes by design, so the two processes do share these files.

fix: With no floor hit, keep the claim (computed = one-way if hits else claim), or skip classification for info packets.
text: `new --door info --range R` on a range with no floor hits is refused. door.classify returns 'two-way' as its baseline (door.py:160), which outranks the 'info' claim, so packet.py promotes the door to two-way. A two-way packet requires a recommended option, so a valid info packet is rejected with exit 1. Reproduced in a scratch repo.

fix: Compile with re.DOTALL (or use [^\0]* instead of .*).
text: Globs compile without re.DOTALL, so the `.*` in `(?:/.*)?$` and `/.*$` stops at a newline. A floor path whose name contains a newline (e.g. `migrations/a\nb.sql`, which git allows and -z passes through) matches no rule and classifies as two-way. The red-team specialist confirmed this in a scratch repo. That breaks the fail-closed guarantee, though it is exotic for non-adversarial lanes.

fix: Use a hard wall-clock deadline, for example a worker thread with join(3) or resolving the host under a timeout, and install an opener that refuses redirects.
text: urlopen(timeout=3) bounds each socket operation, not the call: DNS resolution (MagicDNS down) and a slow-drip server can hold `new`/`close`/`event` well past the 3 s the scope promises. urllib also follows a 301/302 on a POST as a body-less GET; a 200 from that GET counts as sent, so the packet is marked sent but was never stored, e.g. an http:// URL that tailscale serve redirects to https.

fix: Catch OSError/ValueError per item in flush (report and skip), and around the two file reads.
text: flush → try_send reads `<pid>.json` (line 206) with no exception handling. A state file whose packet file is missing or corrupt crashes flush with a traceback and exit 1, and every later packet in the outbox stays unflushed. That contradicts 'harness errors never stop'. `--body-file` (line 264) and `check-reply --file` (line 375) also traceback on an unreadable file instead of the documented exit-1 refusal.

fix: Either have check-reply compare HEAD against head_sha for one-way packets (fail closed), or correct the docstring and have the caller run `stale` before applying a reply.
text: The docstring justifies stale's fail-open with 'applying a reply is gated by check-reply anyway'. check-reply checks only the recorded status and never compares HEAD with head_sha. A packet whose head moved but was never marked stale passes check-reply: the git-unreadable case this sentence covers, or any lane that never calls `stale`.

fix: Floor a path only via the repo file (e.g. `src/billing/` plus `!src/billing/`) and assert one-way.
text: test_negation_line_is_ignored is tautological. `db/migrations/` is already on the defaults floor, so the result is one-way whether or not `!` lines are honoured, and a regression that made negation work would stay green.

fix: Assert state['sent'] is True and 'Blocked' is not in stdout after the re-send; in the flush tests, assert s.posts and the state files.
text: The idempotent-retry test asserts the stub's own dedupe (len(s.posts)==1, where the stub drops 409s). It never asserts that the client treated the 409 as sent: state.sent true, no Blocked note. The flush tests at :173-184 likewise check printed counts but never s.posts or state.

fix: Map each invalid fixture to an expected error substring, and add ui and merged/stale fixtures.
text: test_invalid_fixtures_refused asserts only that errors are non-empty, so a fixture that fails for the wrong reason (a typo in an unrelated field) still passes. There is no `ui` fixture, valid or invalid, and no `merged`/`stale` event fixture, though acceptance asks for fixtures of each type.

fix: Decide in 1.5: default --range to the unit's base..HEAD, or refuse a two-way packet without --range when the lane has commits.
text: Door classification runs only when the caller passes --range, so promote-only protects only callers who opt in. `new --door two-way` on a migration change with no --range goes out as two-way. This may be intended for the skill wiring (Task 1.5) to supply, but nothing in packet.py enforces it.

fix: Pass --ignore-submodules=none (and -c diff.ignoreSubmodules=none).
text: git diff honours diff.ignoreSubmodules and .gitmodules ignore=all, so a submodule pointer bump at a floor path can drop out of the name-status list and classify as two-way.

fix: Translate a leading '!' inside brackets to '^'.
text: The gitignore class `[!x]` (negated) is copied verbatim as the regex class `[!x]`, which matches '!' or 'x', the opposite of the author's intent, so a repo `.one-way-doors` line using it under-matches (fail-open). No default uses brackets.

fix: Use re.fullmatch-safe translation: replace a trailing unescaped `$` with `\Z`, or check with re.search(pattern.replace('$','\Z')).
text: Python's `$` matches before a trailing newline, so `^[0-9a-f]{7,64}$` accepts 'abcdef1\n' and an id 'pk12345678\n' passes the schema (verified). ECMA-262 regex used by standard JSON Schema validators does not, so the queue service's validator may disagree. find_packet's fullmatch then makes such a packet unreachable.

fix: Raise SchemaError when additionalProperties is present and is not False.
text: The docstring says an unsupported construct raises so a schema edit can never silently weaken validation. But `additionalProperties` with any value other than false (true or a sub-schema) is accepted as a known keyword and silently ignored.

fix: Use a directory with no lowercase twin (e.g. ADRS/) and assert the reported path keeps its case.
text: On macOS `git init` sets core.ignorecase=true, so writing DB/Migrations/002.sql into the existing db/migrations/ likely commits the lowercase path. The case-insensitive test may then pass without exercising IGNORECASE.

text: ExecStart hardcodes %h/.local/bin/uv, but on homelab2026 (the only deploy target) uv is /usr/bin/uv and ~/.local/bin/uv does not exist (checked over ssh). The unit fails 203/EXEC and restart-loops every 5 s. install.sh:279 still prints 'enabled decision-queue.service', because `enable --now` on a Type=simple unit succeeds before the exec fails. So the install reports success for a service that never runs (fail-open).

fix: In insert_packet, after a new insert, apply the latest stored closed/stale/touch event for that id in the same transaction (e.g. UPDATE packets ... FROM events WHERE packet_id=%s ORDER BY received_at). Add a test that posts the event before the packet.
reviewer: claude-fallback codex out of credits (per dispatcher)
text: A closed/stale/touch event for a packet the server does not have yet is stored, and its effect is silently dropped. The effect never applies later: insert_packet ignores events already stored, and an event retry is deduplicated (rowcount 0). Reachable path: queue down at `packet.py new` (packet stays in the outbox); queue comes back; Alex answers from the pane; the driver's `close` POSTs the event directly (try_send) before the next `flush` sends the packet. The packet then shows PARKED/open forever and inflates the parked and time-parked stats. The migration comment (events.packet_id 'may arrive before its packet') anticipates this ordering but doesn't handle it.

fix: Move the string out of the expression (`msg = "card failed to render — plain text:\n" + txt` then `{esc(msg)}`), or raise requires-python to >=3.12 and re-lock.
reviewer: claude-fallback codex out of credits (per dispatcher)
text: There is a backslash inside an f-string expression (`{esc("card failed to render — plain text:\n" + txt)}`), which is a SyntaxError before Python 3.12. Confirmed: `ast.parse` under 3.11 fails with 'f-string expression part cannot include a backslash'. pyproject.toml and uv.lock declare requires-python >=3.11, so uv may choose a 3.11 interpreter, and then the whole package fails to import. Homelab currently has 3.14, so this does not affect today's deploy.

fix: Resolve initdb via shutil.which first (plus PG_BIN env override), and make a missing binary a failure unless an explicit opt-out env (e.g. DQ_ALLOW_SKIP_PG=1) is set.
reviewer: claude-fallback codex out of credits (per dispatcher)
text: PGBIN only looks in three hardcoded directories (Homebrew x2, Debian /usr/lib/postgresql/16). When none exists, the session fixture skips every DB-backed test (21 of 23). homelab2026 has no initdb on PATH and no /usr/lib/postgresql, so `pytest -q` there reports only skips, with no failures. Plan 10.1 Task 1.3's acceptance 'service tests green' therefore passes vacuously on the deploy host.

fix: Reject POSTs whose Content-Type is not application/json (forces a CORS preflight the server never answers). For the /views/reset form, also check `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` or Origin.
reviewer: claude-fallback codex out of credits (per dispatcher)
text: This is about cross-site requests, not missing auth (no auth is settled). POST /packets, /events and /views/reset accept any Content-Type. Any web page open in Alex's browser on a tailnet device can forge packets with `fetch(url, {method:'POST', mode:'no-cors', body: JSON})` (text/plain, so no CORS preflight). A forged packet carries a prefilled reply textarea that Alex copies and pastes into an agent pane. That turns a drive-by page into prompt injection into a lane. The attacker needs the MagicDNS hostname, which limits the risk.

fix: Add --frozen to ExecStart (same edit as the blocking ExecStart fix).

If pyproject.toml and uv.lock drift, the service rewrites uv.lock in the repo on start, leaving the checkout dirty (the git-hygiene hook will flag it). fix: Drop "sent" from the state file written by `new`, so the marker is the only record of a send.
text: After 8b96644 the <pid>.sent marker records a send, and nothing writes state['sent'] any more. `new` still writes {"status": "open", "sent": false}, so every state.json says sent=false for its whole life, including packets the queue already holds. The field is dead and misleading to anyone who reads the outbox state (debugging, driver tooling).

fix: In Task 1.5 wiring, state that a lane parked on a one-way packet makes no commits until check-reply passes. Alternatively, compare only the packet's --range paths or the tree, not the commit, if bookkeeping commits must be allowed.
text: The new one-way HEAD check (10.1-r1-07 fix) refuses a reply whenever the lane repo's HEAD differs from head_sha, and the message says to run `stale`, which discards the decision. The scope says one-way lanes park. But a lane that commits bookkeeping while parked (a progress or ledger note, a PARKED marker committed into plans/ in the same repo, as ai-skills' plans are) can then never accept Alex's reply to that packet; it can only stale it and re-emit. This is correct fail-closed behaviour if parked lanes never commit, but nothing enforces or documents that precondition for the Task 1.5 wiring.

fix: Parse it defensively: fall back to 3 on ValueError, or read it inside post().
text: POST_TIMEOUT = float(os.environ.get("PACKET_POST_TIMEOUT") or 3) is evaluated at import, so a non-numeric value makes every command (new, check-reply, flush, ...) die with a traceback before argument parsing. The variable is documented as tests-only, but this is the one place where an environment value breaks the 'harness errors never stop the caller' stance for all subcommands.

fix: Set WorkingDirectory=%h/.local/share/decision-queue or use uv --directory. Correct the equivalent README invocation.
text: The service still cannot import decision_queue. uv --project selects the project without changing directories; the unit has no WorkingDirectory, and pyproject.toml has no build backend to install the package. fix: Acquire the same transaction-scoped lock keyed by packet_id in both insertion paths before inserting or applying effects. Add a deterministic two-connection regression test.
text: Concurrent packet and event transactions can permanently lose the event's effect. The replay SELECT cannot see an uncommitted event, while that event's UPDATE cannot see the uncommitted packet. Both requests then commit successfully; retries return as duplicates without applying the missing close, stale, or touch.

fix: Preserve the original packet content or its canonical digest separately from mutable projection fields, and compare retries against that immutable value.
text: Excluding reversal_cost acknowledges different packet content as an identical retry. Even without any touch event, changing only commits_stacked or as_of returns 200 duplicate:true while discarding the submitted value, violating the new conflict contract.

fix: Define the measurement for packets received after closure and update the timestamp calculation or exclude those samples. Test both statistics endpoints' duration fields for this sequence.
text: Replaying an early closed event sets closed_at before the packet's received_at. stats() subtracts received_at from closed_at, so the newly supported event-before-packet sequence produces negative answer and parked durations.

fix: Fail for an invalid explicit source path and provide a required canonical schema source in the verification environment.
text: The drift guard skips when its source path is wrong, including an explicitly configured DQ_SCHEMA_SOURCE typo. It skipped in this review, so a green test run cannot establish the README's schema-sync claim.

fix: Document identical versus conflicting retries, the new POST refusals, and deferred event replay.
text: The route table still promises 200 for retried packet IDs and says unknown-packet event effects are no-ops. HEAD instead returns 409 for changed packet content and replays stored effects when packets arrive.

fix: Update the prerequisite and opt-out instructions to match the fixture.
text: The test instructions say missing PostgreSQL binaries cause a skip, but conftest.py now fails by default and requires DQ_ALLOW_SKIP_PG=1 for an explicit skip.
